source_records.title: An integrated data-driven and experimental methodology for toroidal propeller design improvement

comparators.description: The study's toroidal prototype at matched required thrust.
The best sampled candidate in the study's design search; used for the reported noise and vortex-coherence comparisons.

claims.condition: Study design condition; matched thrust; 14 parametric design variables.
claims.reported_interpretation: The optimized design reports 7.26% lower power than the study prototype at matched thrust.

claims.condition: Study acoustic directivity analysis; comparison with the best sampled design.
claims.reported_interpretation: The optimized design reports 1.74 dB lower noise than the best sampled design, not necessarily than the prototype or a conventional propeller.

claims.condition: Flow-field analysis of the optimized design and best sampled candidate.
claims.reported_interpretation: Primary vortices are reported to dissipate within 3–4 rotational cycles versus 7–8 cycles for the best sampled design.

limitations: The 7.26% power and 1.74 dB noise results use different comparators.
The paper's design-condition result is not a general mission-level or full-scale vessel improvement.
Raw test traces, geometry files, optimization inputs and redistribution permissions have not been verified in this intake.

source_records.title: Study on the hydrodynamic performance of toroidal propellers

comparators.description: The study's conventional reference propeller for a 14,000-TEU-class container-ship/DTC application.

claims.condition: DTC/container-ship toroidal propeller; cavitation-tunnel tests and DDES CFD.
claims.reported_interpretation: The study reports significantly reduced tip-vortex cavitation and near elimination in the tested configuration.

claims.condition: Study-specific open-water and ship-propulsion comparison.
claims.reported_interpretation: The toroidal propeller is reported to have slightly lower thrust than the conventional reference.

claims.condition: Study-specific open-water comparison.
claims.reported_interpretation: The toroidal propeller is reported to have slightly lower efficiency than the conventional reference.

limitations: This result is a counterexample to universal toroidal superiority, not proof that conventional propellers always win.
Exact numerical deltas and raw cavitation-tunnel data were not verified in this intake.
Results are specific to the studied DTC/container-ship propeller and operating conditions.

source_records.title: Experimental and numerical investigation of cavitation performance in a toroidal propeller

comparators.description: The study's toroidal propeller at its specified open-water operating point; no cross-study comparator is implied.

claims.condition: Advance coefficient J = 1.4; study's tested toroidal configuration.
claims.reported_interpretation: The study reports 70.9% open-water efficiency at J = 1.4; this is not directly comparable with efficiency values at other advance coefficients.

claims.condition: Across the study's advance-coefficient range and vertical-angle adjustments.
claims.reported_interpretation: Cavitation inception type and location vary with advance coefficient; vertical-angle adjustment changes low-pressure regions and cavitation behavior.

limitations: The 70.9% value is tied to J = 1.4 and the study configuration.
Do not rank against a different propeller without matched diameter, Reynolds number, loading, cavitation number and test boundary.
Raw measurements and geometry artifacts were not verified in this intake.

source_records.title: Self-propulsion performance and energy-saving potential of a toroidal propeller for marine applications

comparators.description: KP505 conventional propeller benchmark used in the study's open-water and KCS self-propulsion comparisons.

claims.condition: Advance coefficient J = 0.8; optimized toroidal propeller versus KP505.
claims.reported_interpretation: The paper reports 69.4% efficiency at J = 0.8, about 2% above KP505, with a reported peak of 72.1%.

claims.condition: KCS self-propulsion simulations at model-scale speeds corresponding to full-scale 18, 21 and 24 kn.
claims.reported_interpretation: The study reports 4.14–13.5% lower delivered power than KP505, with the benefit varying by speed.

claims.condition: Study's route and operating-profile assumptions.
claims.reported_interpretation: The study reports 60.97–94.82 t/voyage savings and a 163–239 day payback estimate under its stated scenario assumptions.

limitations: The self-propulsion findings are CFD results, not a physical sea-trial validation.
KCS geometry, speed mapping and route/economic assumptions are study-specific.
Do not promote its numerical savings to another ship or operating profile.

source_records.title: Comparison investigation of hydrodynamic and acoustic performance for metal and flexible marine propeller using experimental method

comparators.description: Metal propeller with identical DTMB 4381 geometry used as the flexible propeller comparator.

claims.condition: Cavitation-tunnel experiment; maximum at high advance coefficients.
claims.reported_interpretation: The paper reports a maximum 43.43% noise reduction; its reported average reduction is 35.22%.

claims.condition: Advance coefficient J = 0.7 to 1.2; cavitating test conditions.
claims.reported_interpretation: The flexible design has an average efficiency reduction of 7.95% relative to the metal design.

claims.condition: At J = 1.2 in the reported test range.
claims.reported_interpretation: The maximum reported efficiency reduction is 21.27% at J = 1.2.

claims.condition: First and second blade-passing-frequency force components in the study's tunnel tests.
claims.reported_interpretation: The paper reports up to 9% lower unsteady axial forces.

limitations: Noise and efficiency results are tied to this flexible metal-TPU shell-core construction and its test conditions.
The result is a trade-off: reduced noise/force does not imply improved efficiency.
Raw data and geometry redistribution permissions were not verified in this intake.

source_records.title: Hydrodynamic performance of a ducted controllable pitch propeller with wavy leading edge

comparators.description: The study's reference ducted controllable-pitch propeller configuration.

claims.condition: Cavitation-tunnel test across three pitch conditions.
claims.reported_interpretation: The paper reports up to 3.5% efficiency improvement for the wavy-leading-edge propeller.

claims.condition: Bollard-pull condition; wavy leading edge applied to the duct.
claims.reported_interpretation: The paper reports improved thrust in bollard-pull condition for the wavy-leading-edge duct.

limitations: The improvement is condition-specific and cannot be promoted to an arbitrary vessel or propulsor.
The reported three pitch settings do not establish performance across a complete mission envelope.
Raw data licensing and exportable geometry are not verified in this intake.

source_records.title: Performance prediction of contra-rotating propellers based on artificial neural network and optimisation technique

comparators.description: KP505 reference propeller in the published design-screening comparison.
Best optimized fixed-pitch propeller from the same model-screening study.

claims.condition: Study's preliminary model-based design screening; not yet independently confirmed by high-fidelity CFD or experiment.
claims.reported_interpretation: The study reports a maximum predicted efficiency of 70.30% versus 65.0% for KP505.

claims.condition: Study's preliminary model-based design screening; not yet independently confirmed by high-fidelity CFD or experiment.
claims.reported_interpretation: The study reports 70.30% versus 66.71% for its best optimized fixed-pitch propeller.

claims.condition: Some high-efficiency candidate solutions in the screened design space.
claims.reported_interpretation: Some high-efficiency candidates marginally violate the cavitation constraint and are reported as near-feasible boundaries, not fully feasible winners.

limitations: This is preliminary model screening, not validated CFD or experimental performance.
Near-feasible cavitation-constraint violations must not be promoted as feasible results.
The article's accepted/in-press status and underlying data availability require review.
